title: Sunny and the Cricket Choir
description: Little Sonny the quokka listens to the crickets begin their nightly song in the bush. A gentle, musical bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Just as the last light was leaving the sky, Sunny heard one cricket begin to sing.

A single, thin, silver note.

Cree.

Sunny sat very still, listening.

Then another cricket joined in. A slightly different pitch, a slightly different rhythm. Cree. Cree.

Then another. And another.

Until, without Sunny quite noticing when it happened, the whole bush was full of crickets singing.

It wasn't loud, exactly. It was everywhere. Like the air itself had started to sing. A high, steady sound that rose and fell and rose again, so many tiny voices weaving together that it sounded like one great, continuous thing.

Sunny lay back in the soft grass and closed his eyes.

He had heard crickets before — every night, all his life. But he had never really listened like this.

It sounded like a choir that had been practicing for a very long time and had finally got it exactly right.

It sounded like the bush saying: the day is done. Be still. Be safe. Rest now.

Sunny felt his whole body relax, one small piece at a time.

His paws uncurled. His shoulders dropped. His breath slowed down to match the slow rhythm of the cricket song.

The stars came out above him, one by one, like tiny instruments joining in.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, cricket choir. Goodnight, long and singing night.
